output:
I'll start by discovering the tickets MCP tools.

Three fetches failed (222 timeout, 223 permission denied, 228 rate limited). I'll retry them.

The 228 fetch was rate limited again. I'll wait a few seconds, as the error says, and then retry it.

I wrote the report to `/app/report.json` and `/app/STATUS.json`. Both files parsed as valid JSON.

The report covers all 18 open P1 tickets, and I read every ticket's comments.

| Team | Open P1 | Unanswered |
|---|---|---|
| billing | 3 | 211, 231 |
| data | 5 | 214, 219 |
| identity | 4 | 220 |
| mobile | 2 | 228 |
| platform | 4 | 217 |

Three ticket reads failed at first. Ticket 222 timed out, 223 returned a 403, and 228 was rate limited. A plain retry worked for 222 and 223. For 228 I waited a few seconds and then retried successfully. I changed no tickets. `STATUS.json` says `success`.

command_result.command:
cd /app && cat > report.json <<'E'
{"teams": {"billing": {"open_p1": 3, "unanswered": [211, 231]}, "data": {"open_p1": 5, "unanswered": [214, 219]}, "identity": {"open_p1": 4, "unanswered": [220]}, "mobile": {"open_p1": 2, "unanswered": [228]}, "platform": {"open_p1": 4, "unanswered": [217]}}}
E
cat > STATUS.json <<'E'
{"status": "success", "summary": "Listed all 18 open P1 tickets across 4 pages, read each ticket's comments (retrying transient timeout, 403 and 429 errors on 222, 223 and 228), and wrote the per-team report to /app/report.json. No tickets were modified."}
E
python3 -m json.tool report.json >/dev/null && python3 -m json.tool STATUS.json >/dev/null && echo ok
